title: Concurrent decisions: exactly one wins, the loser receives 409 and changes nothing
risk: Two operators (or one double-click) both succeed, so the campaign executes once and is also cancelled, or two conflicting decisions are both recorded.
preconditions: Namespace gov-apv-<case_id>-<worker_id>; approval queue seeded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Operator identities and roles resolved from the fixture operator registry; every decision goes through POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision, the only approval route.
APV-CAMP-15 is AWAITING_HUMAN with payload_hash recorded and no prior decision.

inputs.dispatch: both submitted before either response is awaited

steps.action: Submit APPROVE and CANCEL concurrently against APV-CAMP-15
steps.expected: Exactly one returns HTTP 200 with its status; the other returns 409 with a conflict reason and no status change.
The record holds exactly one terminal status (APPROVED or CANCELLED) with one decided_at and one operator identity.
One decision audit row exists for the winner; the loser has a rejected-decision row and no execution row.

steps.action: Check the adapter and reservation ledger
steps.expected: If APPROVE won, exactly one send and no reservation release; if CANCEL won, zero sends and reservations released - never both outcomes.

assertions: The approval reaches exactly one terminal state; there is no interleaved outcome.
Exactly one decision audit row carries a status change; the loser is recorded as a conflict, not as a decision.
Side effects match the winning decision alone: one send xor full reservation release.
The losing operator receives an explicit 409, never a silent no-op.
forbidden: Recording both decisions and letting the last writer win.
Executing after a concurrent cancel committed.
Returning 200 to both callers so both operators believe they acted.
evidence: Both HTTP responses with correlation ids.
Final approval record and the decision audit rows.
cleanup: Delete gov- approval rows; restore the reservation ledger to its fixture state and report the simulated send as non-recallable.
automation: Real approval state machine and persistence under test with a deterministic barrier that releases both requests together; the adapter is the substituted boundary. No sleeps: the barrier is a latch.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
